question: What is the average speed of a bus which covers half the distance at a speed of 72 km/hr and the other half at a speed of 90 km/hr?3565
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal distances → Average speed = (2ab)/(a + b)

= (2 × 72 × 90)/(72 + 90)

= 12960/162

= 80 km/hr

**∴ Answer = 80 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ = 72 km/hr, Speed₂ = 90 km/hr (equal distances)

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let total distance = 2d

⇒ Time₁ = d/72

⇒ Time₂ = d/90

⇒ Total time = d/72 + d/90

⇒ LCM = 360 → Total time = (5d + 4d)/360 = 9d/360 = d/40

⇒ Average speed = 2d ÷ (d/40)

⇒ = 2d × 40/d = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Distance Rule

Average speed = (2ab)/(a + b)

Harmonic Mean

Average speed for equal distances is harmonic mean of speeds.

Time Formula

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Common Mistake

Do not take simple average (72 + 90)/2.
